Our existing owned-site pipeline remains valued at approximately $24.0bn, with stronger operating economics largely absorbed by the revised financing and terminal-value framework. Importantly, we already include the full 800 MW of critical IT load associated with the 1 GW campus in our base case pipeline valuation. The incremental positive is greater visibility into power availability and a shorter interval between initial deployment and subsequent expansion. Text: $APLD Today's selloff was sentiment driven with the market lumping every neocloud and AI data center name into one basket. The credit says otherwise. $CRWV unsecured bonds spooked the sector, but APLD's campus debt is different. It's project level, secured by real estate, power and long dated take or pay leases. CRWV borrows against GPUs that depreciate fast. $CIFR and $WULF rely on Fluidstack leases with Google backstopping rent for warrants. APLD's campuses are financed with secured project debt instead. PF3 and DF1 are 15 year take or pay leases with an IG hyperscaler as direct tenant. If it's Meta as widely believed, that's the weaker end. Meta sits in the lower half of the four candidates on credit and is still AA range. PF3 and DF still need funding, but 100 bps wider is only about $10M a year per $1B raised, and stabilized campuses can refinance into cheaper ABS later. Private credit is also an option, and an IG tenant lets those deals price on their own merits.
